title: Application-layer protocols
intro: Questions on FTP, DHCP, ICMP, and ARP — four protocols that appear constantly in packet captures and are essential to understand for both troubleshooting and security analysis.

questions.prompt: In active FTP, which side initiates the data connection: the client or the server?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **Active FTP**: the client sends `PORT <IP,port>` on the control channel. The **server** then initiates a TCP connection from port 20 to the client's specified address. This breaks through NAT because the server cannot reach the private client IP — the reason passive mode was introduced.

questions.prompt: In passive FTP, which side initiates the data connection: the client or the server?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **Passive FTP**: the client sends `PASV`. The server responds with an IP:port. The **client** then connects to that port. Because the client initiates all TCP connections, passive mode works through NAT and most firewalls. EPSV (extended passive) is the modern variant.

questions.prompt: What are the four DHCP messages in the DORA process, in order?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
```
Client → broadcast: DHCPDISCOVER  (who can give me an address?)
Server → broadcast: DHCPOFFER     (I can offer 192.168.1.50)
Client → broadcast: DHCPREQUEST   (I accept 192.168.1.50 from that server)
Server → broadcast: DHCPACK       (confirmed, lease for 86400s)
```
Broadcast is used throughout so multiple DHCP servers can see the exchange. DHCP relay agents forward DORA across subnets.

questions.prompt: What ICMP type number is an Echo Request (the packet sent by ping)?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **ICMP type 8** — Echo Request. The target responds with **type 0** — Echo Reply. Both carry an Identifier and Sequence Number to match requests to responses. `ping` increments the sequence number each second. Firewalls that block ICMP type 8 prevent ping but not TCP/UDP connectivity.

questions.prompt: What ICMP type number signals that a packet was discarded because its TTL field reached zero in transit?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **ICMP type 11** — Time Exceeded (code 0: TTL Exceeded in Transit). The router that decrements TTL to zero drops the packet and sends this back to the original source. **traceroute** exploits this by sending packets with TTL=1, 2, 3… and recording which routers generate type 11 responses.

questions.prompt: What ICMP type number indicates that a destination is unreachable?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
**ICMP type 3** — Destination Unreachable. Key codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Net unreachable |
| 1 | Host unreachable |
| 2 | Protocol unreachable |
| 3 | Port unreachable |
| 4 | Fragmentation needed (Path MTU Discovery) |
| 13 | Administratively prohibited |

Code 3 (port unreachable) is returned when UDP hits a closed port. Code 4 is critical for PMTUD — blocking it causes black-hole routing.

questions.prompt: What protocol resolves an IPv4 address to a hardware (MAC) address on a local network segment?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **ARP (Address Resolution Protocol, [RFC 826](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc826))**. A host broadcasts `who has 192.168.1.1? tell 192.168.1.50`. The owner of that IP unicasts back `192.168.1.1 is at aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff`. The result is cached in the ARP table (`arp -n` or `ip neigh`). ARP only works within a broadcast domain — inter-subnet traffic uses the default gateway's MAC.

questions.prompt: What term describes an ARP reply sent without a preceding ARP request, used to announce a new IP-to-MAC binding and update neighbour caches?
questions.solutionMarkdown:
**Gratuitous ARP** — the sender claims its own IP as both the source and target. Used by:
- HSRP/VRRP virtual routers on failover to update switches
- Virtual machines migrating between hosts
- Hosts reconfiguring their IP

Attackers use gratuitous ARP for ARP poisoning / man-in-the-middle attacks — override a legitimate IP:MAC mapping in neighbours' caches.

questions.prompt: What UDP port does a DHCP server listen on?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **UDP 67** (server) and **UDP 68** (client). The client sends from 68 to the broadcast address on port 67. DHCP relay agents ([RFC 3046](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3046)) forward requests to a remote server, inserting the Option 82 circuit-ID so the server can assign the correct subnet.

questions.prompt: What ICMP type number is sent by a router to tell a host to use a different first-hop router for a specific destination?
questions.solutionMarkdown: **ICMP type 5** — Redirect. A router sends this when it receives a packet from a host and knows a better next-hop on the same subnet. The host should update its routing cache. ICMP redirects are often disabled in hardened environments because they can be abused to poison host routing tables.

summaryMarkdown:
## ICMP type quick reference

Defined in [RFC 792](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc792) (IPv4) and [RFC 4443](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4443) (IPv6). Full type/code registry: [IANA ICMP Parameters](https://www.iana.org/assignments/icmp-parameters/icmp-parameters.xhtml)


| Type | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | Echo Reply |
| 3 | Destination Unreachable |
| 5 | Redirect |
| 8 | Echo Request |
| 11 | Time Exceeded |
| 12 | Parameter Problem |

## ARP vs NDP

IPv6 replaces ARP with **NDP (Neighbour Discovery Protocol)**, which uses ICMPv6 messages:
- Type 135: Neighbour Solicitation (≈ ARP request)
- Type 136: Neighbour Advertisement (≈ ARP reply)

NDP also handles router discovery and SLAAC (stateless address autoconfiguration).
